transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We're here for the readiness review on the real-time collaboration service ahead of Monday's 09:00 UTC production launch. As I understand it, the service passed its staging tests — functional, failover, and basic load — and the draft launch plan currently enables the feature for 10% of accounts initially, permits up to 10,000 concurrent connections, uses the client library's default 5-second retry interval, stores collaboration data in the primary production region, and retains session transcripts for 90 days. Before I finalize and record the binding policy, I want to give backend engineering, reliability, privacy, and customer success each a chance to do their final check-in. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a concern with the retry interval in the draft plan. While investigating an unrelated mobile performance report this afternoon, I confirmed that mobile clients resume from background in bursts and currently retry every 5 seconds, which can create a reconnect storm. The rollout policy should set the retry interval to exactly 30 seconds instead of using the client library's default 5 seconds. I have not yet filed the client-library ticket for this.

transcript.text: I need to flag a capacity concern before we finalize. About 20 minutes ago, I completed a production-traffic replay and confirmed that the collaboration cluster's safe connection ceiling for Monday is exactly 6,000 concurrent connections — not the 10,000 currently in the draft plan. The autoscaling limit hasn't been updated yet because the replay results are still being attached to the capacity worksheet. We need to lower the concurrent connection cap to 6,000 before Maya records the binding policy.

transcript.text: I need to flag two privacy compliance issues with the draft plan. I completed a privacy review this morning and confirmed that collaboration content for EU accounts must remain in the EU processing region — the current plan stores all collaboration data in the primary production region, which would violate that requirement. Additionally, session transcripts must be deleted after exactly 30 days, not the 90 days currently in the draft plan. I haven't opened the compliance ticket yet because legal was still reviewing the wording, but these two items need to be corrected before Maya records the binding policy.

transcript.text: I need to flag a customer-success concern before we finalize. I reconciled the customer-success rollout spreadsheet an hour ago and confirmed that six accounts — acct-204, acct-219, acct-233, acct-241, acct-278, and acct-301 — have administrator opt-out commitments until their enablement sessions are complete. Those six accounts must be excluded from Monday's rollout. I have not updated the launch checklist yet, so we need to make sure these exclusions are reflected in the binding policy before Maya records it.
